findings.finding: The August 2024 revisions of JDF 612 and JDF 615 interleaved their glyph runs, so extracted text was scrambled. The July 1, 2025 revisions this build binds read back cleanly.
findings.consequence: The build asserts each form's printed title reads back literally on page 1, and records the printed line at every widget's coordinate in reports/caption-evidence.json beside Colorado's authored field name. Placement is still rastered for the visual reviewer.

findings.finding: C.R.S. § 24-72-706 reaches a conviction by two branches, and section 5 of JDF 612 asks which one applies.
findings.consequence: The branch is a participant election rather than a route-determined selection: it turns on the offence's own class and on whether this district attorney consents, and a packet that ticked one would be swearing to a legal characterisation of a conviction the build has not seen. The route the packet WAS built for is stated in the field map, the source receipt and the participant instructions.

findings.finding: Section 3 of JDF 615 is the court's own findings, and the July 2025 revision prints "The Court Completes the Rest of this Form" above it.
findings.consequence: All four are left blank under the court-owned refusal class. A proposed order that pre-ticked the finding the judge is being asked to make would be drafting the ruling rather than requesting it.

findings.finding: Section 4 of JDF 612 asks what the conviction was, when sentence was imposed and when supervision ended, and the platform holds none of the three.
findings.consequence: Each is declared REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and named to the participant in participant-instructions.md, with the clerk of the convicting court as the place to get it. None is estimated: a sentencing date guessed onto a sworn motion is worse than a blank one.

findings.finding: JDF 612 asks the movant for the agencies holding records, while JDF 615 repeats record-recipient fields inside the court's numbered order body.
findings.consequence: The motion's agency names, case numbers and addresses are declared REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and named to the participant. JDF 615's numbered body remains court-owned because JDF 611 directs the filer to complete only sections A–C.

findings.finding: JDF 612 R: July 1, 2025 prints the Colorado Bureau of Investigation as "(Required)" and ships its box (3C) unticked. The August 2024 revision shipped that box ticked.
findings.consequence: The box is a participant election, and the instructions tell the participant to tick it; this build does not tick it. The census still reads each control's value from the pinned source, so a source-carried default is recorded as a documentAuthoredAppearance rather than as ink on a refused field.

findings.finding: No mounted custody held the July 1, 2025 revisions of JDF 612 and JDF 615 that legal-design-track-registry.json records as current. The issuer's live URL answered HTTP 403.
findings.consequence: Both are bound from retained issuer bytes under reference/co-jdf-2025-07-01/ by exact SHA-256 — 4a45070b9332e73ddbb3ec9cb8d326b707589856d3104b8ab7d9ab991d9d496b for JDF 612 and 184a33faf5d800a189f4c0fbd180912a02888d60e1100ca586064a8c753a0a26 for JDF 615 — the digests the track registry records. The bytes came from Internet Archive captures of the issuer URLs; the source receipt records each capture.

findings.finding: The August 2024 JDF 612 shipped twenty-three text widgets with the annotation Hidden flag set. The July 2025 revision ships none.
findings.consequence: The census still reads the flags from the pinned binary and the build asserts that no write lands on a hidden widget. Because 3Z.1, the court case number in section 3, is now visible, the case number the packet holds is written there; under the 2024 revision it was carried to the participant. The shared descriptors read the silent name 3Z.1 as charge-table row 1, so the build names the fact for that one field through the finalizer's single-fact narrative channel, the channel IA DCI-77 and AZ use for the same gap.

findings.finding: JDF 612 R: July 1, 2025 asks for the address on two lines, "Mailing Address:" and "City, State, & Zip:", while JDF 205 has separate street, city, state and ZIP fields.
findings.consequence: JDF 612 receives participant.street_address and the composed participant.city_state_zip; JDF 205 receives the structured street, city, state and ZIP facts separately, so neither form omits or duplicates parts.

findings.finding: The July 2025 JDF 612 renumbers its sections (6–12 become 3–9), removes the psilocybin question and the counsel Esq./registration fields, merges Division and Courtroom, splits the certificate-of-service recipient, and adds an interpreter question and a court-attendance choice. Earlier map labels for Group_9A, Group_9C and Group_10 named questions the form does not print there.
findings.consequence: The dictionary follows the 2025 widget set exactly, asserted in both directions. Group_9A, Group_9C and Group_10 now carry the questions the form prints (automatic sealing, restitution owed, criminal history attached). Intake asks no interpreter or attendance question, so both are participant elections left blank.

findings.finding: JDF 205's Email widget is 167.56pt wide. The complete boundary email exceeds its usable width under Helvetica at the 6pt readable floor, while Times-Roman fits at that same floor.
findings.consequence: Only that field is eligible for the governed standard-font fallback. The finalizer tries Helvetica first, uses Times-Roman only after the measured refusal, and reads the complete exact value back from the flattened bytes. Any value that still fails both fonts remains unfittable and now increments knownRequiredFieldsMissing instead of disappearing behind the canonical map.
